---
title: Keep files on a device
description: Read a file's bytes from a working copy, choose how much disk the copy's files take, keep attachments there offline, and find out why one is missing.
---

A [working copy](/build/devices) holds items, not their bytes. It fetches a [file's](/build/files) bytes when something reads them, keeps them in a file cache beside the store, and keeps the files attached to items it holds so they're there offline.

The CLI examples use `marfa device`, with the copy named by `--db` or `MARFA_DB`, as [Write in a working copy](/build/write-in-a-working-copy) shows. In the Swift examples, `copy` is an [open working copy](/swift-sdk/working-copy#open-a-copy). [Handle files](/build/handle-files) covers uploading bytes and pointing an item at them.

## Read a file's bytes

Ask for the bytes by the hash in the file item's `blob_ref`. The copy fetches them first if it doesn't hold them:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa device blobs get sha256:51e9f5829f49ee68908ca90c92606e36e6e55e1b95ba39a77ab239a0589d89c8
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let bytes = try await copy.blobs.withFile(hash) { url in try Data(contentsOf: url) }
```

The CLI prints the path of the file it holds. `withFile` calls your closure with it, and the file stays put only while the closure runs: **read it inside the closure**, and copy it out if it must outlast the call.

A reading handle, or a copy without a server, can't fetch, so it refuses a file it doesn't hold with `bytes_absent`.

## Choose how much disk files take

The copy keeps the files it fetched within a **file budget**. Past it, a trim removes the files read longest ago, and a later read fetches them again. The default is the larger of 2 GiB and a tenth of the volume, held to what leaves a twentieth of the volume free.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa device blobs budget 5000000000
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let removed = try await copy.blobs.setBudget(.bytes(bytes: 5_000_000_000))
```

Setting a budget trims to it at once and reports the bytes removed, and the store keeps the choice. The CLI also takes `default` and `keep-all`, and the Swift SDK `.default` and `.keepAll`. `marfa device blobs budget` with no value shows the budget in force. A file larger than the budget is still fetched when asked for.

**To empty the file cache without changing the budget**, such as for a "Remove downloaded files" button, a Swift app calls `copy.blobs.removeFetchedFiles()`. It removes every file the copy can fetch again and reports the bytes removed. Attachments kept offline, uploads not yet sent and files being read stay. The CLI has no command for it.

## Keep attachments offline

**A file attached to an item the copy holds stays on the device**, outside the budget, and a trim never takes it. Fetch every one the copy lacks after a hydration and after each catch-up:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device blobs fetch-kept
```

```text
fetched 1 attached file(s), 18 byte(s)
```

</Terminal>

In Swift, the same fetch is `try await copy.blobs.fetchKept()`.

It fetches the smallest files first and waits out a server that asks for a wait of a minute or less. It stops at the first file the disk has no room for, once the server can't be reached, or once the server asks for a longer wait, and passes over a file that fails otherwise. Control-C, or canceling the task, stops it, and the files already fetched stay.

**A fetch that stops part way keeps the bytes it received** as a partial file, which the copy never answers as the file. The next fetch asks the server for a new link and requests the rest. A partial file that isn't an attachment's counts toward the budget, and the copy removes one left untouched for seven days.

## When a fetch is refused

A fetch that can't keep the file whole refuses with one of these codes:

| Code | Swift | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no_room` | `noRoom` | The volume can't hold the rest of the file. It refuses before receiving any byte, naming the file's size and the bytes free. |
| `storage_full` | `storageFull` | The volume filled while the bytes were written. The copy keeps none of them. |
| `bytes_absent` | `bytesAbsent` | The server holds no bytes by that hash or can't be reached, or the link sends more bytes than the file item's `size_bytes`. |
| `decoding` | `decoding` | The bytes don't hash to the file's name. The copy keeps none of them. |

## Find out why an attachment is missing

`marfa device status` counts the attachments the copy holds whole and the ones it lacks, grouped by why. These are the last lines of its output:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device status
```

```text
file budget default, in force 6573915136 byte(s)
files held 0 byte(s)
attached files held 0, 0 byte(s) outside the budget
attached files not held 1, 18 byte(s)
  not fetched yet: 1, 18 byte(s)
```

</Terminal>

Under `--json` the groups are `file_cache.attachments.not_held_by_reason`, each with a `reason`, the count of `attachments`, the `bytes` they state and how many are `unstated`. The Swift SDK reads the same counts from [`blobs.cache()`](/swift-sdk/files#what-the-cache-reports).

| `reason` | The CLI says | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not_fetched` | not fetched yet | Run `fetch-kept`. |
| `no_room` | no room on the disk | Make room on the disk, then run `fetch-kept`. |
| `unreachable` | the server could not be reached | Run `fetch-kept` once the server answers. |
| `rate_limited` | the server asked for a longer wait | Run `fetch-kept` later. |
| `absent` | the server holds none | The server holds no bytes by that hash. Nothing on the device brings it back. |
| `failed` | the fetch failed | Run `fetch-kept` again. |
| `not_in_copy` | the file is outside the slice | The copy holds the edge but not the file item. Hydrate the file's type. |

On Apple platforms, the copy also keeps fetched files out of backups.

The rules behind this guide are in the [device](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/device.md) chapter of the contract.
